episodes.label: Regulated Cell Death Paradigm (Apoptosis, Ferroptosis, Pyroptosis & Necroptosis) — Eukaryotic cell demise is not merely passive accidental lysis; cells execute multiple genetically encoded, biochemically distinct Regulated Cell Death (RCD) subroutines—immunologically silent caspase-driven apoptosis versus lytic, inflammatory necroptosis (RIPK3–MLKL), pyroptosis (Gasdermins), and metabolic iron-lipid-peroxidation ferroptosis (GPX4).
episodes.notes: The multi-modal Regulated Cell Death paradigm is entrenched foundational consensus across developmental biology, immunology, oncology, and neurodegeneration. Over the past 15 years it completely shattered the classical binary dichotomy ('programmed apoptosis vs. accidental necrosis') by decoding molecular executioners for lytic pathways—MLKL pores in necroptosis, Gasdermin D/E pores in pyroptosis, GPX4/FSP1/7-DHC lipid-peroxidation brakes in ferroptosis, and copper-mitochondrial cuproptosis (Tsvetkov 2022). Active 2026 research centers on pathway plasticity and backup crosstalk ('PANoptosis' multiprotein complexes) where blocking one executioner (e.g. caspase-8 inhibition by a virus) triggers compensatory necroptosis or pyroptosis.

episodes.label: Autophagy & Proteostasis Network Theory of Cellular Quality Control — Cellular proteome integrity is sustained by an integrated, stress-responsive Proteostasis Network coupling molecular chaperones, the ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS), and selective/bulk macroautophagy (ATG–lysosome degradation) to clear misfolded aggregates and damaged organelles—whose progressive age-related collapse drives neurodegenerative and metabolic disease.
episodes.notes: The integrated Proteostasis Network and ATG-mediated autophagy–lysosome machinery stand as foundational consensus in cell biology, honored by Nobel Prizes for both ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis (2004) and yeast ATG autophagy genetics (Ohsumi 2016) and deepened by atomic understanding of selective organelle clearance (PINK1–Parkin mitophagy, ER-phagy, aggrephagy) and lipid-transfer ATG2/ATG9 phagophore expansion. Clinical translation has forced critical mechanistic nuance: in oncology, autophagy is sharply double-edged (suppressing genomic instability before transformation while fueling survival and immune evasion of established RAS/pancreatic tumors), and in neurodegeneration, simply boosting autophagosome initiation when downstream lysosomal acidification is choked worsens proteotoxic traffic jams.

episodes.label: High-Energy Chemical-Intermediate Hypothesis of Oxidative Phosphorylation — Analogous to substrate-level phosphorylation in glycolysis (1,3-bisphosphoglycerate), mitochondrial respiratory electron transfer was hypothesized by E. C. Slater to generate a discrete covalent high-energy chemical intermediate (A~I -> X~P) that directly transfers phosphate to ADP without involving transmembrane electrochemical ion gradients.
episodes.notes: Completely falsified and superseded by Peter Mitchell's Chemiosmotic Theory, yet treasured across philosophy of science and biochemistry as one of biology's sharpest historical cautionary anchors. For more than two decades (1953–1974), the world's foremost bioenergeticists failed to isolate the phantom covalent 'X~P' intermediate despite exhaustive fractionation—until Jagendorf's acid-bath chloroplasts and Racker & Stoeckenius's chimeric bacteriorhodopsin–ATP synthase liposomes proved that structurally unrelated proton pumps couple to ATP synthase solely through a sealed membrane and transmembrane proton-motive force.

episodes.label: Hormones or Brain Circuits? — The Carbohydrate–Insulin Model (CIM) vs. the Modern Brain-Centric Energy-Balance Model (EBM), Ultra-Processed Foods, Protein Leverage & the GLP-1 Crucible
episodes.notes: Quoting the First Law of Thermodynamics explains the global obesity pandemic about as well as quoting the conservation of people explains why a lecture hall got crowded. This five-act adversarial deep dive stages the fiercest causal-arrow battle in modern clinical physiology: does high-glycemic-load food elevate postprandial insulin to trap fuels inside adipocytes and secondarily trigger hunger and sluggish metabolism (the Carbohydrate–Insulin Model championed by David Ludwig and Cara Ebbeling), or do involuntary brain circuits responding to energy-dense, fast-eating ultra-processed food environments drive positive energy balance and secondary fat deposition (the modern brain-centric Energy-Balance Model articulated by Kevin Hall, Sadaf Farooqi, Jeffrey Friedman, Ruth Loos, and John Speakman)? Walk quantitatively through all seven verified landmark papers — from the 20-week Framingham State Food Study (BMJ 2018) and the NuSI metabolic-chamber trial (AJCN 2016) to the +508 kcal/day ultra-processed food trial (Cell Metabolism 2019), the -689 kcal/day low-fat versus ketogenic NIH inpatient showdown (Nature Medicine 2021), human CNS BMI genetics (Science 2021), and the 2023–2026 GLP-1/GIP incretin crucible. Pause twice at the chalkboard to derive the 7.5-to-9.2-fold first-week ketogenic glycogen–water scale illusion, the Weir CO2 respiratory-quotient sensitivity of doubly labeled water, and the exact paired-crossover power and energy-density budget needed for a decisive 8-week head-to-head trial.

theory.canonical_title: Carbohydrate–Insulin Model vs. Energy-Balance Model of Obesity
theory.core_claim: The Carbohydrate–Insulin Model (Ludwig, Ebbeling) posits that high-glycemic-load carbohydrates raise postprandial insulin-to-glucagon ratios, trapping metabolic fuels inside adipocytes and secondarily driving compensatory hunger and suppressed energy expenditure—whereas the modern Energy-Balance Model (Hall, Speakman, Friedman) holds that brain-centric hypothalamic and reward responses to energy-dense, ultra-processed food environments drive positive energy balance and secondary fat deposition.
theory.verdict_2026: While formally contested in active peer-reviewed exchanges, the empirical balance in 2026 tilts heavily toward the modern brain-centric Energy-Balance Model (EBM) as the primary driver of population obesity. Direct NIH metabolic-ward adversarial trials (Hall et al. 2016 AJCN; Hall et al. 2019 Cell Metabolism; Hall et al. 2021 Nature Medicine) falsified core CIM predictions: lowering insulin by >50 percent on an isocaloric ketogenic diet slightly slowed body-fat loss, while an ad libitum low-fat, high-glycemic-load plant diet produced ~689 kcal/day LESS intake and greater body-fat loss than an animal ketogenic diet. Furthermore, GLP-1/GIP incretin agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide) produce 15–22 percent weight loss by acting on CNS appetite circuits even while potentiating meal-stimulated insulin secretion. CIM proponents counter that metabolic-ward trials are too brief (<4 weeks) for keto-adaptation and that Ebbeling et al. (2018 BMJ) observed higher doubly labeled water expenditure during low-carb weight-loss maintenance, keeping mechanistic debate alive around hyperinsulinemic subgroups.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: CIM advocates routinely caricature the modern Energy-Balance Model as naive moralistic 'eat less, move more' willpower advice, ignoring that Hall, Farooqi & Friedman's EBM explicitly models involuntary neuroendocrine regulation (leptin, melanocortin, GLP-1, ultra-processed palatability/energy-density dynamics). Conversely, simplistic 'calorie-is-a-calorie' critiques ignore genuine macronutrient effects on satiety, diet-induced thermogenesis, and postprandial glycemia in insulin-resistant individuals.

historical_evolution.milestone: Ludwig & Friedman formalize the modern Carbohydrate–Insulin Model; Hall (2016) tests isocaloric keto in metabolic chambers while Ebbeling/Ludwig (2018 BMJ) report elevated DLW expenditure on low-carb maintenance.
Hall's inpatient RCTs demonstrate ultra-processed diets drive +508 kcal/day overeating (2019) and low-fat high-carb beats ketogenic diets for ad libitum fat loss (2021 Nature Medicine).
Flagship rival manifestos appear side-by-side in AJCN (Ludwig et al. 2021 CIM; Hall et al. 2022 EBM) alongside Speakman & Hall's Science critique.

Transformative human weight loss from CNS-acting GLP-1/GIP agonists (which boost glucose-dependent insulin secretion) strongly supports brain-first energy-intake regulation, while CIM tests focus on long-duration hyperinsulinemic cohorts.

theory.falsification_criteria: The CIM would be decisively vindicated—and EBM falsified—if long-term (>12-week) metabolic-ward trials matching energy density, protein, and ultra-processing prove that lowering glycemic load alone produces markedly lower ad libitum caloric intake and greater body-fat loss mediated strictly by declining insulin rather than protein/fiber satiety.

theory.stealth_refute: Your study shows participants on a higher-insulin, low-fat minimally processed diet spontaneously consume fewer calories and lose equal or more body fat than on a low-insulin ketogenic diet, OR shows ultra-processed food texture/energy density drives weight gain independent of insulin.

episodes.label: Germ Theory of Infectious Disease — Specific transmissible diseases are caused by colonization, replication, or toxin production by specific microscopic pathogens (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, helminths, and prions), establishable via epidemiological, microbiological, or sequence-based causal criteria (Koch's and Falkow's postulates).
episodes.notes: Germ Theory is one of the most successful, life-saving foundational consensuses in human history—underpinning antisepsis, vaccination, antibiotics, antivirals, and molecular diagnostics, and repeatedly expanding into formerly 'non-infectious' conditions (Helicobacter pylori in peptic ulcers, HPV in cervical cancer, Epstein–Barr virus as a near-obligate trigger of multiple sclerosis, Bjornevik et al. 2022 Science). Modern microbiology has refined rigid nineteenth-century 'one microbe = one disease' Koch postulates into Casadevall & Pirofski's Damage-Response Framework and polymicrobial/dysbiosis ecology, recognizing that clinical outcome reflects the dynamic interaction of microbial virulence, host genetics, immune calibration, and commensal communities.

episodes.label: Somatic Mutation Theory (SMT) vs. Tissue Organization Field Theory (TOFT) of Cancer — The Somatic Mutation Theory (SMT) holds that cancer originates from sequential clonal accumulation of genetic/epigenetic driver mutations within a single somatic cell lineage, whereas the Tissue Organization Field Theory (TOFT; Sonnenschein & Soto) contends cancer is a tissue-level disruption of reciprocal stromal–epithelial morphogenetic fields where mutations are secondary byproducts.
episodes.notes: Somatic Mutation Theory remains the dominant foundation of modern oncology—overwhelmingly validated by hereditary cancer-suppressor syndromes (BRCA1/2, RB1, APC, TP53), mutational signatures, and precision oncogene-targeted drugs (imatinib for BCR-ABL, osimertinib for EGFR, sotorasib for KRAS G12C) that directly falsify TOFT's strict claim that driver mutations are mere epiphenomena. However, naive cell-autonomous SMT ('mutations alone automatically equal cancer') has undergone a profound paradigm refinement since 2015: deep sequencing of histologically normal aging human skin, esophagus, and lung (Martincorena 2015, 2018; Hill & Swanton 2023 Nature) revealed dense carpets of canonical NOTCH1, TP53, KRAS, and EGFR driver clones that remain benign until microenvironmental promoters (PM2.5 macrophage IL-1beta, chronic inflammation, aging stroma) unlock malignant expansion—integrating somatic mutation with Berenblum's classic promotion and tissue-field ecology.

episodes.label: Warburg Effect & Metabolic Reprogramming Theory of Tumorigenesis — Proliferating tumors avidly ferment glucose into lactate even under normoxia (the Warburg Effect)—originally hypothesized by Otto Warburg to stem from irreversible mitochondrial respiratory failure, and reinterpreted in modern oncology as oncogene-driven metabolic reprogramming supplying anabolic carbon, redox balance, and epigenetic oncometabolites.
episodes.notes: Metabolic reprogramming is an undisputed hallmark of cancer—powering clinical FDG-PET imaging and FDA-approved oncometabolite inhibitors (IDH1/2 inhibitors blocking 2-hydroxyglutarate)—yet Otto Warburg's original causal hypothesis ('irreversible mitochondrial injury causes cancer') is definitively refuted for most malignancies, because nearly all tumors retain intact, functional mitochondria required for aspartate synthesis, pyrimidine biogenesis, and metastatic survival. At the same time, direct in vivo isotope-tracing measurements (Bartman, Rabinowitz et al. 2023 Nature) brought a stunning modern twist: primary solid tumors actually suppress TCA-cycle ATP production (partly confirming slow respiration in vivo while conserving ATP by downregulating tissue-specific physiological functions), whereas migrating metastases markedly UP-regulate mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.

episodes.label: Amyloid Cascade Hypothesis of Alzheimer's Disease — Imbalanced production or impaired clearance of amyloid-beta (Abeta42) peptides and oligomers in the brain initiates a linear downstream cascade—triggering tau hyperphosphorylation, neurofibrillary tangles, neuroinflammation, synaptic loss, and clinical Alzheimer's dementia.

episodes.label: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (Barker / DOHaD Hypothesis) — Adverse nutritional, endocrine, or environmental exposures during critical intrauterine and early-postnatal windows permanently 'program' organ structure (nephron/beta-cell endowment) and epigenetic metabolic regulation, elevating adult risk of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease—especially upon postnatal caloric mismatch.
episodes.notes: DOHaD is a major, well-established framework in developmental physiology and preventive medicine, corroborated by animal uteroplacental-restriction experiments, natural-experiment famine cohorts (Dutch Hunger Winter, Chinese Famine), and organ-endowment deficits (reduced nephron number causing hypertension). However, modern human genetic epidemiology has enforced a critical quantitative correction: structural equation modeling and Mendelian randomization across >300,000 mother–offspring pairs (Warrington et al. 2019 Nature Genetics; Moen et al. 2020) proved that a large proportion of the observational inverse link between low birth weight and adult cardiometabolic disease reflects shared fetal pleiotropic genetics (Hattersley & Tooke's 1999 'Fetal Insulin Hypothesis') rather than pure intrauterine deprivation—while evolutionary Predictive Adaptive Response (PAR) claims have faced heavy skepticism compared to direct developmental-constraint deficits.

episodes.label: Allostasis & Allostatic Load vs. Classical Cannon Homeostasis — Rather than passively correcting errors around rigid fixed physiological setpoints (Cannon's Homeostasis), the brain achieves physiological stability through predictive, feedforward parameter regulation matched to anticipated demand (Sterling & Eyer's Allostasis), whose chronic activation imposes cumulative multisystem wear-and-tear (McEwen's Allostatic Load).
episodes.notes: Predictive feedforward physiological regulation (interoceptive active inference, cephalic-phase insulin secretion, circadian blood-pressure and cortisol anticipation) paired with stress-induced multisystem wear-and-tear is widely entrenched across neuroendocrinology, psychoneuroimmunology, and computational neuroscience in 2026. Yet rigorous systems physiologists (Day 2005; Ramsay & Woods 2014 Psychological Review) have forced important conceptual precision: classical homeostasis was never restricted to rigid fixed setpoints (Cannon himself recognized anticipatory autonomic activation, and Mrosovsky's 1990 'rheostasis' already modeled shifting regulated setpoints like fever), while clinical 'allostatic load' composite scores still suffer from arbitrary biomarker weighting and non-standardized cutoff definitions across epidemiological studies.

episodes.label: ApoB / LDL Causal Lipid Theory of Atherosclerosis — Retention of apolipoprotein-B-containing lipoproteins (LDL, VLDL remnants, IDL, Lp(a)) within the arterial subendothelial intima is the necessary, dose-dependent causal initiator of atherosclerotic plaque formation—scaling log-linearly with cumulative lifetime plasma ApoB/LDL exposure and amplified by endothelial injury and vascular inflammation.
episodes.notes: The causal role of ApoB-containing lipoproteins in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is one of the strongest multi-evidence consensuses in all of clinical medicine (Ference et al. 2017 European Heart Journal EAS Consensus), converging identically across monogenic diseases (FH LDLR/APOB/PCSK9 gain-of-function vs. protective PCSK9/NPC1L1 loss-of-function), >200 prospective cohorts, Mendelian randomization, and randomized outcomes trials across four mechanistically distinct lipid-lowering classes (statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, bempedoic acid) showing ~22 percent relative risk reduction per 1 mmol/L LDL-C drop regardless of drug mechanism. Modern 2026 clinical refinement emphasizes (1) total atherogenic particle count (ApoB) and Lp(a) over LDL-C mass alone (Sniderman 2019), and (2) parallel targeting of residual inflammatory risk (IL-1beta CANTOS, colchicine LoDoCo2) that acts downstream of intimal lipoprotein trapping.

episodes.label: Monoamine Deficiency Hypothesis of Major Depressive Disorder — Major depressive disorder (MDD) is caused by a primary quantitative deficiency of synaptic monoamine neurotransmitters—serotonin (5-HT), norepinephrine, and/or dopamine—which conventional antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, tricyclics) directly correct by elevating synaptic monoamine concentrations.
episodes.notes: The simple 'chemical-imbalance / baseline monoamine deficiency' hypothesis has been decisively challenged and abandoned as a standalone etiology by contemporary biological psychiatry, even though monoaminergic drugs remain clinically effective above placebo for moderate-to-severe MDD (Cipriani 2018 Lancet). Crucially, SSRIs raise synaptic serotonin within hours yet require 2–6 weeks for clinical remission; acute tryptophan depletion does not induce depression in healthy unmedicated volunteers; and Moncrieff et al.'s (2022 Molecular Psychiatry) widely debated umbrella review underscored the absence of consistent direct baseline serotonin-deficiency biomarkers (though Jauhar et al. 2023 noted altered 5-HT release capacity in PET challenges). In 2026, psychiatric neuroscience has pivoted to Neuroplasticity / Synaptic-Connectivity (BDNF–TrkB, mTORC1, rapid-acting glutamatergic ketamine/esketamine, GABAergic zuranolone) and immuno-metabolic network-circuit models in which monoamines act merely as one upstream modulator of plasticity.

episodes.label: Hallmarks & Information Theory of Aging vs. Stochastic Damage Accumulation — Contemporary geroscience competes between (1) multi-factorial damage-accumulation catalogs (the 12 Hallmarks of Aging; stochastic somatic mutations, crosslinks, and metabolic wear), (2) the Information Theory of Aging (Sinclair) positing that aging is primarily reversible loss of analog epigenetic chromatin information driven by DNA-repair relocalization, and (3) developmental-hyperfunction / multi-cause models.
episodes.notes: The mechanistic causal hierarchy of mammalian aging remains intensely contested in 2026. While the 12 Hallmarks of Aging (Lopez-Otin et al. 2013, 2023 Cell) serve as the universal organizing map of geroscience, critics (Gems & de Magalhaes 2021) rightly note it is a descriptive taxonomy rather than a predictive causal theory explaining which upstream driver initiates the cascade. David Sinclair's Information Theory of Aging (Yang et al. 2023 Cell)—showing inducible non-mutagenic DNA double-strand breaks (ICE mice) accelerate epigenetic aging and partial OSK Yamanaka reprogramming restores youthful methylation/vision—sparked massive excitement and equally sharp pushback: leading aging geneticists (Gladyshev, Vijg, Schumacher, Brenner) argue that irreversible somatic DNA mutations (which scale tightly across mammalian lifespans, Cagan et al. 2022 Nature), telomere/aneuploidy loss, extracellular-matrix elastin/collagen crosslinking, and senescent-cell niches cannot be erased by epigenetic reprogramming alone, and that ICE-mouse break induction introduces non-physiological chromatin trauma.

episodes.label: Humoral Pathology & Miasma Theories of Disease — Classical Western medicine explained internal illness as dyscrasia (imbalance) among four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile (Hippocrates/Galen)—while epidemic outbreaks were attributed to miasmas ('bad air' and putrefactive vapors rising from swamps and filth) rather than specific replicating biological agents.
episodes.notes: Completely falsified and superseded by cellular pathology (Virchow), Germ Theory (Pasteur, Koch), and modern molecular physiology—yet retained in the Atlas for two enduring epistemic lessons. First, miasma theory illustrates 'right intervention for the wrong mechanism': nineteenth-century sanitary reformers (Chadwick, Nightingale) built sewers, ventilated wards, and drained marshes to banish bad smells, inadvertently slashing cholera, typhoid, and malaria transmission and delaying recognition that the underlying theory was false. Second, humoral equilibrium thinking persists subtly in alternative 'detox/balance' wellness rhetoric and even oversimplified mainstream metaphors like 'chemical imbalance' in psychiatry and endocrinology.

episodes.label: Strangers, Alarms, or Sudden Change? — Janeway's Infectious Non-Self (PRR/PAMP) vs. Matzinger's Danger Theory (DAMP) vs. Pradeu–Vivier's Discontinuity Theory & Cytosolic Guard Immunity
episodes.notes: An immune system that literally obeyed the textbook rule 'attack all non-self' would wage fatal war on 38 trillion gut bacteria, every meal you swallow, and every developing human fetus. This five-act three-way adversarial deep dive pits immunology's three grand unifying theories against one another across eight verified landmark papers: Charles Janeway's 1989 'immunologist's dirty little secret' predicting germline Pattern Recognition Receptors (experimentally vindicated by Ruslan Medzhitov and Elizabeth Kopp's Toll-like receptor synthesis); Polly Matzinger's 1994 and 2002 Danger Model centering endogenous tissue necrosis alarms (biochemically confirmed by Yan Shi, James Evans, and Kenneth Rock's 2003 isolation of monosodium urate crystals from dying cells); and the sharp cross-examination led by Russell Vance (2000), Thomas Pradeu and Edwin Cooper (2012), and Pradeu, Sébastien Jaeger, and Eric Vivier's 2013 Discontinuity Theory proposing that immune receptors act as temporal change detectors firing on abrupt motif shifts while adapting to persistent signals. Pause twice at the chalkboard to derive the 2.4-fold necrotic monosodium urate supersaturation switch versus 8.3-million-fold higher TLR4 endotoxin sensitivity (showing why 1 part-per-million LPS hijacks sterile DAMP assays), compute the 672-fold ramp-rate discontinuity ratio at equal cumulative dose, and engineer a pre-registered 120-mouse germ-free factorial knockout experiment bridging PRRs, DAMPs, cytosolic guard sensors, and temporal kinetics.

theory.canonical_title: Self/Non-Self Pattern Recognition vs. Danger Theory vs. Discontinuity Theory
theory.core_claim: Janeway's Pattern Recognition model proposes that germline-encoded receptors (PRRs) gate adaptive immunity by sensing conserved microbial molecular patterns (PAMPs); Matzinger's Danger Theory counters that endogenous alarm signals from stressed or necrotic tissues (DAMPs) drive immune activation regardless of foreignness, while Pradeu's Discontinuity Theory posits that immune receptors fire on abrupt temporal shifts in molecular motifs and adapt to persistent signals.
theory.verdict_2026: No single grand criterion accounts for every immunological outcome in 2026, leaving the three frameworks in productive, unresolved competition at the conceptual level even as molecular biology integrates their parts. PRR-mediated PAMP detection (TLRs, NLRs, cGAS–STING) and DAMP-driven sterile inflammation (HMGB1, ATP, uric acid crystals) are both experimentally bedrock, yet neither alone explains why necrotic tumors evade rejection, why benign allogeneic grafts trigger fierce immunity without necrosis, or why dense gut commensals carrying canonical PAMPs are actively tolerated. Discontinuity Theory and newer 'effector-triggered immunity' (guard hypothesis) syntheses increasingly explain temporal tolerance and mucosal homeostasis, but remain hotly debated regarding how quantitative discontinuity thresholds map onto receptor biophysics.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely invoke 'self vs. non-self' as an unproblematic textbook binary while ignoring commensal tolerance and maternal–fetal chimerism, or invoke 'danger signals' circularly—defining any molecule that activates dendritic cells as a DAMP after the fact. Researchers also frequently neglect how tissue-resident barrier context and rate-of-change kinetics (discontinuity) override static ligand identity.

historical_evolution.milestone: Burnet formalizes clonal self/non-self discrimination; Charles Janeway exposes 'the immunologist's dirty little secret' (adjuvants) and predicts pattern recognition receptors for infectious non-self.
Polly Matzinger launches the Danger Model centering endogenous tissue distress; Ruslan Medzhitov and Janeway clone human TLR4, empirically vindicating PRR-gated costimulation.

Kenneth Rock identifies monosodium urate as a canonical necrotic DAMP; Thomas Pradeu and Eric Vivier propose Discontinuity Theory to unify commensal tolerance, chronic infection exhaustion, and tumor immune editing.

Discovery of cytosolic guard sensors (pyrin, NLRP1) and tissue-specific macrophage tolerogenic circuits pushes immunology toward hybrid PAMP–DAMP–discontinuity–guard architectures rather than a single universal trigger.

episodes.label: Clonal Selection Theory of Adaptive Immunity (Burnet / Talmage) — Each naive B and T lymphocyte expresses a single, pre-committed antigen receptor generated stochastically prior to antigen encounter; binding of cognate antigen selectively expands that clone into effector and memory progeny while autoreactive clones are purged or silenced during development.
episodes.notes: Clonal Selection remains the unshakeable bedrock of vertebrate adaptive immunology, corroborated by Susumu Tonegawa's V(D)J recombination genetics, germinal-center somatic hypermutation imaging, and modern single-cell VDJ sequencing of millions of clones. Key classical corollaries have been substantially enriched rather than overturned: central deletion is now understood to be leaky, requiring Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs), receptor editing, and peripheral anergy to prevent autoimmunity, and antigen receptors are proven to be polyspecific (cross-reactive) rather than strictly monospecific.

episodes.label: Hygiene & 'Old Friends' Microbiota Hypothesis of Allergy & Autoimmunity — Reduced early-life exposure to coevolved commensal microbes, environmental saprophytes, and helminths ('Old Friends') impairs maturation of regulatory T-cell networks and epithelial barriers, leaving the immune system biased toward hyper-reactive Th2 allergic inflammation and loss of self-tolerance.
episodes.notes: The original 1989 'hygiene' framing—blaming personal cleanliness and acute childhood viral infections—has been substantially revised into Graham Rook's 'Old Friends' and 'biodiversity' hypothesis, which holds strong empirical support across farming-cohort studies (Amish vs. Hutterite), germ-free mouse models, and infant gut-microbiome longitudinal cohorts. However, randomized clinical trials of probiotics and therapeutic helminth colonization for established asthma, IBD, and multiple sclerosis have yielded mostly null or modest results, showing that timing (critical early-life windows), diet/short-chain fatty acids, and epithelial barrier pollutants (detergents, microplastics, ultra-processed emulsifiers) act jointly with microbial depletion.

episodes.label: Trained Immunity (Epigenetic Innate Immune Memory) — Innate immune cells (monocytes, macrophages, NK cells) and their bone-marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) undergo durable metabolic rewiring and histone chromatin remodeling (e.g., H3K4me3, H3K27ac) after microbial or sterile challenge, producing enhanced, antigen-nonspecific heterologous responsiveness to unrelated secondary insults for months to years.
episodes.notes: Trained immunity is firmly established in 2026 as a major pillar revising the classical textbook dogma that immunological memory is exclusively adaptive, supported by mechanistic studies of BCG, beta-glucan, and oxidized LDL driving glycolysis, mevalonate-pathway signaling, and HSPC myelopoiesis bias. Active refinement centers on boundary conditions: large randomized trials of BCG against COVID-19 (BRACE trial, 2023) failed to show heterologous protection in adults, demonstrating that trained immunity is context-, age-, pathogen-, and tissue-specific—and can become maladaptive in atherosclerosis, neuroinflammation, and post-sepsis organ injury.

episodes.label: Cancer Immunoediting (Elimination–Equilibrium–Escape) — The immune system plays a dual host-protective and tumor-sculpting role through three sequential phases—Elimination (immunosurveillance), Equilibrium (immune-enforced dormancy), and Escape—selecting for poorly immunogenic tumor variants via neoantigen loss, MHC-I downregulation, and immunosuppressive microenvironment remodeling.
episodes.notes: Cancer Immunoediting is the dominant organizing framework of modern immuno-oncology, powerfully vindicated by checkpoint blockade (anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-1), Rag2-deficient mouse transplant experiments, and longitudinal human tumor genomics (TRACERx) revealing HLA loss-of-heterozygosity and neoantigen depletion under T-cell pressure. Yet 2026 genomic analyses show that classic linear three-phase selection does not operate uniformly: many human cancers exhibit 'neutral' subclonal evolution or intrinsic immune exclusion (Wnt/beta-catenin, stromal fibrosis) from inception without an identifiable elimination phase, and chronic inflammation actively promotes tumorigenesis prior to immune editing.

theory.canonical_title: Cancer Immunoediting (Elimination–Equilibrium–Escape)
theory.core_claim: The immune system plays a dual host-protective and tumor-sculpting role through three sequential phases—Elimination (immunosurveillance), Equilibrium (immune-enforced dormancy), and Escape—selecting for poorly immunogenic tumor variants via neoantigen loss, MHC-I downregulation, and immunosuppressive microenvironment remodeling.
theory.verdict_2026: Cancer Immunoediting is the dominant organizing framework of modern immuno-oncology, powerfully vindicated by checkpoint blockade (anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-1), Rag2-deficient mouse transplant experiments, and longitudinal human tumor genomics (TRACERx) revealing HLA loss-of-heterozygosity and neoantigen depletion under T-cell pressure. Yet 2026 genomic analyses show that classic linear three-phase selection does not operate uniformly: many human cancers exhibit 'neutral' subclonal evolution or intrinsic immune exclusion (Wnt/beta-catenin, stromal fibrosis) from inception without an identifiable elimination phase, and chronic inflammation actively promotes tumorigenesis prior to immune editing.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely treat high tumor mutational burden (TMB) as synonymous with strong immunoediting and checkpoint sensitivity, ignoring that subclonal passenger mutations trigger poor T-cell control compared to clonal truncal neoantigens and that many 'cold' tumors evade immunity via physical exclusion rather than antigen editing. Investigators also conflate transplantable carcinogen-induced mouse sarcomas (hyper-immunogenic) with autochthonous low-mutation human epithelial cancers.

historical_evolution.milestone: Burnet and Lewis Thomas formulate cancer immunosurveillance, which falls into skepticism after Osias Stutman observes no increased spontaneous tumor incidence in athymic nude mice.

Robert Schreiber, Lloyd Old, and Gavin Dunn rescue and expand the theory into Cancer Immunoediting using Rag2-/- and IFN-gamma-deficient mice, proving tumors grown in immunodeficient hosts are rejected by immunocompetent hosts.
Clinical triumph of Allison and Honjo's immune checkpoint inhibitors proves dormant anti-tumor T-cell responses exist in humans and can reverse the Escape phase.

Pan-cancer evolutionary genomics (TRACERx, Hartwig) distinguishes actively immunoedited tumors (HLA LOH, B2M mutation, neoantigen depletion) from inherently immune-desert and neutrally evolving tumors.

episodes.label: Virulence–Transmission Trade-Off Hypothesis — Natural selection does not inevitably drive pathogens toward benign commensalism; instead, it maximizes basic reproduction number (R0) at an intermediate level of virulence because higher within-host replication increases transmission rate per unit time while simultaneously shortening the infectious period via host mortality or immobilization.
episodes.notes: The trade-off hypothesis successfully overthrew the naive pre-1980s 'avirulence dogma' and exhibits classic empirical vindication in systems like rabbit myxomatosis, HIV set-point viral load (Fraser et al.), and Marek's disease in vaccinated poultry (Read et al.). Nevertheless, it remains contested as a general predictive law in 2026: SARS-CoV-2 variant evolution (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) underscored how pre-symptomatic/asymptomatic transmission decouples late host mortality from onward spread, while short-sighted within-host evolution, dead-end spillover hosts, antigenic immune escape, and coincidental virulence frequently dominate over simple R0–mortality curves.

Andrew Read and colleagues show imperfect ('leaky') Marek's disease vaccines preserve host survival while permitting transmission of hyper-virulent strains, providing experimental proof of trade-off release.

SARS-CoV-2 waves (more virulent Delta followed by antigenically shifted Omicron) expose the primacy of immune escape, tropism shifts, and pre-symptomatic transmission decoupling over naive virulence–mortality trade-offs.

episodes.label: Holobiont & Hologenome Theory of Evolution — A multicellular host and its resident microbial consortium (the holobiont) together with their combined genetic repertoire (the hologenome) constitute a primary, cohesive unit of natural selection, capable of rapid adaptive evolution via microbial acquisition, abundance shifts, and vertical or pseudo-vertical transmission.
episodes.notes: While the ecological reality of host–microbiome interdependence (the holobiont as an ecological/physiological unit) is universally accepted, the stronger evolutionary claim that the hologenome routinely acts as a Darwinian unit of selection remains sharply contested in 2026. Strict vertical fidelity holds in obligate insect endosymbionts (Buchnera–aphid, Wolbachia), justifying multilevel holobiont selection there; however, for vertebrates and corals whose microbiomes are predominantly acquired horizontally from the environment, evolutionary theorists (Douglas, Werren, Moran, Sloan) argue that divergent evolutionary interests and low partner fidelity make standard host–microbe coevolution and community ecology far more explanatory than treating the hologenome as a single organism.

theory.common_paper_blindspot: Microbiome papers frequently invoke 'holobiont evolution' whenever a gut microbe confers a metabolic benefit on a host, silently conflating ecological mutualism or host-mediated partner filtering with unified Darwinian selection on a heritable hologenome. Seth Bordenstein and Kevin Theis expand the framework, arguing phylosymbiosis and hybrid lethality demonstrate hologenomic speciation across animals and plants.

Nancy Moran, Daniel Sloan, Angela Douglas, and John Werren publish trenchant critiques showing that low microbial heritability and rampant horizontal transmission invalidate the hologenome as a general unit of selection.

Quantitative population-genetic models (Roughgarden, Lloyd, Suárez) shift the debate from all-or-nothing rhetoric to measuring exact vertical-vs-horizontal transmission ratios and trait-group selection across specific host lineages.

episodes.label: Quorum Sensing & Sociomicrobiology Theory — Bacteria synthesize, secrete, and detect diffusible signaling molecules (autoinducers such as AHLs, oligopeptides, and AI-2) to coordinate collective gene expression—including virulence, biofilm formation, competence, and public-goods secretion—once local signal concentration surpasses a threshold, creating social dilemmas governed by kin selection and cheater policing.
episodes.notes: Quorum sensing and sociomicrobiology form a foundational consensus that completely overturned the 20th-century view of bacteria as solitary, asocial unicells. Mechanistic circuits (LuxI/LuxR, Agr, Las/Rhl, AI-2, and even phage arbitrium peptides) are resolved at atomic and single-cell precision; ongoing refinement recognizes Rosemary Redfield's 'diffusion sensing' and 'efficiency sensing' insights—demonstrating that autoinducer accumulation simultaneously integrates cell density, physical confinement, and mass-transfer flow rather than counting cell numbers in isolation.

Matthew Parsek, E. Peter Greenberg, Stuart West, and Stephen Diggle establish sociomicrobiology, demonstrating public-goods cooperation, social cheating, and kin-selection maintenance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Discovery of phage-encoded 'arbitrium' quorum peptides governing lysis–lysogeny decisions (Sorek) and host-sensing interkingdom quorum crosstalk expands sociomicrobiology across viruses and eukaryotic hosts.

episodes.label: Antibiotic Persistence, Tolerance & Phenotypic Bet-Hedging — Clonal bacterial populations survive lethal bactericidal antibiotic exposure without acquiring genetic resistance mutations by entering reversible, metabolically arrested or slow-growing phenotypic states—either population-wide (tolerance) or in a small stochastic/triggered subpopulation (persistence)—that act as evolutionary bet-hedging and stepping stones to canonical resistance.
episodes.notes: The distinction between resistance (elevated MIC), tolerance (elevated MDK99 across the whole population), and persistence (biphasic killing curve with a surviving subpopulation at unchanged MIC) is now consensus (Balaban et al. 2019), and longitudinal clinical isolates confirm that tolerance mutations consistently accelerate the subsequent evolution of high-level genetic resistance. At the molecular level, however, earlier toxin–antitoxin (TA) locus models suffered major retractions and failed replications (notably the 10-TA deletion E. coli story in 2017–2018 due to phi80 phage contamination), shifting 2026 mechanistic focus to intracellular ATP depletion, protein aggregation, stringent-response (ppGpp) dormancy, and active efflux heterogeneity.

episodes.label: Original Antigenic Sin & Immune Imprinting — The immune system's first exposure to a drifting pathogen (such as influenza or SARS-CoV-2) permanently biases subsequent humoral and cellular responses toward cross-reactive memory B cells targeting epitopes of the priming strain, accelerating recall immunity while potentially blunting de novo naive B-cell responses to mutated epitopes on antigenically drifted variants.
episodes.notes: Original Antigenic Sin—modernized and de-pejoratized as 'immune imprinting' or 'antigenic seniority'—is robustly corroborated by birth-cohort influenza epidemiology (Gostic et al. 2016 showing lifelong protection against severe H5N1/H7N9 tracks childhood hemagglutinin-group priming) and single-cell germinal-center fate mapping during SARS-CoV-2 Omicron boosting. Crucially, 2023–2026 human studies refuted the fatalistic assumption that imprinting permanently locks out new responses: repeated exposure to antigenically distant monovalent variants (e.g., XBB.1.5 or JN.1) progressively recruits naive B cells and drives somatic hypermutation of imprinted clones toward breadth, showing that imprinting is often protective rather than purely 'sinful.'

episodes.label: Jerne's Idiotypic Network Theory of Immune Regulation — Because the variable regions (idiotopes) of antibodies and lymphocyte receptors are themselves immunogenic, the adaptive immune system operates as a closed, self-referential web of anti-idiotypic interactions (Ab1 -> Ab2 -> Ab3) whose endogenous dynamic equilibria—rather than external foreign antigens alone—govern immune memory, self-tolerance, and activation.
episodes.notes: As a master explanatory framework for physiological immune regulation, memory, and self-tolerance, Niels Jerne's Idiotypic Network Theory has been definitively superseded by MHC-restricted T-cell help, PRR/costimulation gating, Foxp3+ regulatory T cells, and long-lived bone-marrow plasma/memory cells. Although anti-idiotypic antibodies genuinely exist (and occasionally appear in autoimmunity, IVIG immunomodulation, or anti-drug antibody responses), Melvin Cohn's devastating theoretical critiques and knockout-mouse genetics proved that spontaneous idiotypic cascades do not control physiological repertoire selection or memory maintenance; the theory endures as a historic anchor for network-systems immunology.

episodes.label: Front vs. Back of the Brain — Global Neuronal Workspace (GNWT) vs. Integrated Information Theory (IIT), the 2025 Nature Cogitate Adversarial Trial, No-Report Paradigms, PCI Bedside Diagnostics & the Phi Falsifiability Storm
episodes.notes: Why do 69 billion neurons in the human cerebellum generate zero conscious experience while 16 billion neurons in the cerebral cortex conjure an entire subjective universe? This five-act adversarial deep dive puts neuroscience's two heavyweight theories of consciousness on public trial: Stanislas Dehaene and Jean-Pierre Changeux's Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT), which locates conscious access in a late 300-millisecond nonlinear broadcast across frontoparietal pyramidal networks, against Giulio Tononi, Christof Koch, and Marcello Massimini's Integrated Information Theory (IIT), which derives consciousness axiomatically from maximal irreducible cause-effect power (Phi) inside a sustained posterior cortical hot zone. Walk through all eight verified landmark papers—from Tononi's 2008 Provisional Manifesto, Dehaene & Changeux (Neuron 2011), Casali et al.'s bedside Perturbational Complexity Index breakthrough (Science Translational Medicine 2013), Tononi et al. (Nature Reviews Neuroscience 2016), and Mashour et al. (Neuron 2020), into the sharpest adversarial shocks: Boly et al.'s (Journal of Neuroscience 2017) no-report demolition of P3b and prefrontal report confounds, the 2023 open letter by 124 researchers questioning IIT's falsifiability, and the landmark 256-participant multimodal Cogitate Consortium adversarial collaboration (Ferrante et al., Nature 2025) that wounded both theories simultaneously. Pause twice for step-by-step calculations—first proving why computing exact Phi across just 100 neurons takes over 20,000 years on an exascale supercomputer while Lempel-Ziv PCI compresses cortical responses in milliseconds, and second engineering the electrode coverage and trial count needed to lift sparse prefrontal iEEG statistical power from 26 percent to 99 percent—before weighing rival Recurrent Processing, Higher-Order Perceptual Reality Monitoring, and Dendritic Integration frameworks and arming working researchers with a stealth-assay field guide.

theory.canonical_title: Global Neuronal Workspace (GNWT) vs. Integrated Information Theory (IIT) — Cogitate Adversarial Showdown
theory.core_claim: Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (Baars, Dehaene, Changeux) posits that conscious access arises when sensory representations trigger a late (~300 ms) nonlinear 'ignition' broadcasting information across frontoparietal long-range pyramidal networks; Integrated Information Theory (Tononi, Koch) instead identifies phenomenal experience with maximal irreducible cause-effect power (Phi) located primarily in a sustained posterior-cortex 'hot zone.'
theory.verdict_2026: The landmark Cogitate Consortium preregistered adversarial collaboration (Melloni et al., Nature 2025; 256 participants across fMRI, MEG, and intracranial EEG) delivered a sobering split verdict that left neither flagship theory unscathed. IIT passed predictions of sustained category- and orientation-specific decoding in posterior occipito-temporal cortex throughout stimulus duration, yet failed its core prediction of sustained inter-areal posterior synchronization; GNWT found some prefrontal decoding for stimulus category, yet failed to observe predicted stimulus-offset ignition or orientation decoding in prefrontal cortex—keeping consciousness neuroscience deeply contested in 2026 alongside intense methodological disputes over IIT's Phi computability and pseudoscience allegations (Fleming et al. 2023).
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Papers routinely conflate Ned Block's distinction between 'access consciousness' (reportable cognitive availability, GNWT's target) and 'phenomenal consciousness' (subjective experiential quality, IIT's target), treating behavioral report correlates like the P3b ERP as pure consciousness signatures when no-report paradigms show they track task reporting instead. Authors also often treat clinical Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) scores as direct measurements of IIT's mathematical Phi, even though PCI is an empirical Lempel-Ziv compressibility heuristic compatible with multiple rival theories.

historical_evolution.milestone: Bernard Baars proposes cognitive Global Workspace Theory; Stanislas Dehaene and Jean-Pierre Changeux ground it in frontoparietal cortical ignition, while Giulio Tononi publishes the first axiomatic formulation of IIT.

Dehaene & Changeux canonize GNWT ignition markers; Marcello Massimini and Tononi validate the Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) in unresponsive patients, while Koch et al. champion the posterior cortical 'hot zone' using no-report paradigms.

Templeton-funded Cogitate Consortium launches preregistered adversarial testing co-designed by Dehaene and Tononi; 124 researchers publish a widely debated open letter challenging IIT 4.0's falsifiability and panpsychist entailments.

Cogitate Consortium publishes full multimodal adversarial results in Nature (2025), forcing both GNWT and IIT camps into major mechanistic revisions while energizing middle-ground recurrent, predictive, and thalamocortical theories.

theory.falsification_criteria: Decisive discrimination under no-report paradigms requires showing either (a) full phenomenal experience persists when prefrontal broadcast/ignition is reversibly silenced (falsifying strict prefrontal GNWT), or (b) structurally distinct feedforward networks with near-zero Phi produce identical subjective experience, or posterior cortical causal integration fails to track conscious content switches (falsifying IIT).
theory.stealth_support: Your study detects nonlinear late (~300 ms) frontoparietal broadcast ignition tracking conscious perception even without motor report (supporting GNWT) — OR sustained posterior sensory-area integration and high perturbational complexity tracking subjective duration (supporting IIT).
theory.stealth_refute: Your study finds prefrontal decoding/P3b vanishes under no-report paradigms or lacks stimulus-offset ignition (challenging GNWT), OR fails to find sustained inter-areal posterior synchronization across stimulus duration (challenging IIT, as in Cogitate 2025).

head_to_head.theory_a_prediction: Conscious perception triggers nonlinear late (~250–350 ms) ignition at BOTH stimulus onset AND offset in prefrontal-parietal cortex with content-specific decoding in PFC even in task-irrelevant no-report trials.
head_to_head.rival_b_prediction: Conscious content and duration are encoded strictly in sustained, maximally integrated posterior sensory-parietal-occipital ('hot zone') reciprocal connectivity throughout the entire perceptual duration, independent of prefrontal ignition.
head_to_head.confounder_trap: Motor-report / working-memory contamination (making prefrontal task-execution look like consciousness) and low spatial-temporal resolution scalp EEG blurring posterior vs. frontal generators.

episodes.label: Hebbian Plasticity, LTP & Synaptic Engram Theory of Memory — Long-term memories are physically encoded as activity-dependent modifications of synaptic weights—canonical NMDA-receptor-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP) and depression (LTD)—linking co-active neuronal ensembles ('engram cells') that reactivate together during recall.
episodes.notes: Synaptic plasticity and optogenetically verifiable engram ensembles represent the dominant mechanistic framework for memory in 2026, powerfully demonstrated by Malinow's bidirectional optogenetic erasure/restoration of fear memory via LTD/LTP (Nabavi et al. 2014) and Tonegawa/Josselyn engram activation experiments. However, the classic purely synaptic Hebbian paradigm is undergoing intense mechanistic revision: behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity (BTSP, Magee 2017) forms place fields in a single trial over seconds rather than millisecond STDP windows; silent engrams survive protein-synthesis inhibition (Ryan/Tonegawa 2015); and continuous 'representational drift' in cortex and hippocampus forces models to explain stable memory despite constant synaptic turnover and intrinsic excitability changes.

episodes.label: Predictive Processing & the Free Energy Principle (Friston / Clark) — The cortex implements a hierarchical generative model that continuously issues top-down sensory predictions and propagates only precision-weighted prediction errors upward (Rao & Ballard); Karl Friston's Free Energy Principle generalizes this via active inference into a mathematical imperative asserting that all self-organizing biological systems persist by minimizing variational free energy across a Markov blanket.
episodes.notes: In 2026, it is crucial to separate two radically different epistemic tiers: concrete circuit-level Predictive Coding (hierarchical mismatch neurons in visual V1, auditory mismatch negativity, motor efference copy) is strongly supported in specific cortical loops (e.g., Georg Keller's sensorimotor mismatch neurons in mouse V1), though canonical microcircuit laminar assignments remain contested against classic feedforward feature-hierarchy and hybrid models. By contrast, the overarching Free Energy Principle (FEP) as a grand unified theory of brain and life faces intense mathematical and philosophical critique (Raja et al., Bruineberg, Bowers, Aguilera et al.): critics argue FEP is an unfalsifiable tautological mathematical formalism ('repackaged Bayes/control theory') whose Markov-blanket physics rarely yields unique empirical brain predictions not already derivable from reinforcement learning or optimal control.

episodes.label: Higher-Order Thought (HOT) & Recurrent Processing Theories of Consciousness — Higher-Order Theories (Rosenthal, Lau, Brown) assert that a first-order sensory representation becomes conscious only when indexed or monitored by a higher-order metacognitive representation in prefrontal cortex; Recurrent Processing Theory (Lamme) counters that local horizontal and top-down feedback loops within sensory cortex suffice for rich phenomenal awareness even without prefrontal access or reportability.
episodes.notes: Following the 2025 Cogitate stalemate between GNWT and IIT, Higher-Order Theories (especially Hakwan Lau's Perceptual Reality Monitoring, PRM) and Victor Lamme's Recurrent Processing Theory (RPT) have surged as the sharpest mechanistic rivals in consciousness science. Both command compelling experimental pillars—blindsight and prefrontal TMS metacognitive dissociations bolster HOT/PRM, whereas backward-masking disruption of early visual feedback (~100 ms) and Iconic Memory (Sperling) overflow experiments support RPT—yet both remain deadlocked over whether unreportable local recurrence truly carries subjective qualia or merely pre-conscious sensory readiness.

episodes.label: Dopamine Reward Prediction Error (RPE) & Temporal-Difference Theory — Phasic firing of midbrain dopamine neurons in the VTA and SNc broadcasts a scalar temporal-difference reward prediction error (actual minus expected reward, delta) to striatum and prefrontal cortex, serving as the teaching signal that updates action values via corticostriatal synaptic plasticity.
episodes.notes: The Schultz–Dayan–Montague dopamine RPE hypothesis stands as one of the greatest triumphs of computational neuroscience—validated across primate electrophysiology, rodent optogenetics, and human neuroimaging—yet has undergone profound functional diversification by 2026. Modern fiber photometry and single-cell recordings prove midbrain dopamine is not a uniform global scalar broadcast: distinct anatomical subpopulations simultaneously encode distributional RL quantiles (Dabney/Uchida 2020), movement kinematics/vigor (SNc), perceived novelty/threat in the tail of the striatum (Menegas/Watabe-Uchida), and ramping value/state-prediction errors (Berke, Gershman), alongside Kent Berridge's classic 'wanting vs. liking' incentive-salience dissociation.

episodes.label: Complementary Learning Systems (Hippocampal–Neocortical Consolidation) — Intelligent brains avoid catastrophic interference by pairing two specialized learning systems: a fast, sparse, pattern-separated hippocampal index that rapidly encodes unique episodes, and a slow, interleaved neocortical network that extracts statistical regularities via offline sharp-wave ripple replay during sleep.
episodes.notes: Complementary Learning Systems (CLS; McClelland, McNaughton & O'Reilly 1995) remains the dominant computational and neurobiological framework for systems memory consolidation, corroborated by hippocampal replay during slow-wave sleep, amnesia gradients (patient H.M.), and deep-learning experience-replay architectures. episodes.label: Neural Population Dynamics & Low-Dimensional Cortical Manifolds — Rather than single neurons acting as static tuned encoders of external stimuli or muscle forces, cortical circuits operate as recurrent dynamical systems whose collective firing trajectories evolve across low-dimensional neural manifolds—including output-null preparatory subspaces—constrained by underlying synaptic connectivity.
episodes.notes: The 'computation through dynamics' / neural manifold framework (Shenoy, Churchland, Gallego, Sadtler) has become the dominant paradigm in motor, prefrontal, and cognitive systems neuroscience, powerfully supported by brain-computer interface (BCI) learning constraints (monkeys rapidly learn within-manifold perturbations but struggle for days on outside-manifold mappings) and conserved latent manifolds across days despite single-neuron drift. Active refinement in 2026 challenges simplistic low-dimensionality claims: Stringer et al. (Nature 2019) proved visual cortex V1 population codes are high-dimensional with a power-law eigenvalue spectrum (~1/n) balancing capacity and smoothness, and critics warn that PCA/jPCA rotational trajectories can be mathematical artifacts of smooth sequential/Gaussian-process tuning curves in low-complexity lab tasks.

episodes.label: Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR / Quantum Microtubule Consciousness) — Consciousness arises not from classical synaptic computation alone, but from non-computable quantum gravitational wave-function collapse ('objective reduction') orchestrated inside coherent quantum superposition states of neuronal cytoskeletal microtubule tubulin dimers.
episodes.notes: Orch-OR remains heavily challenged and outside mainstream neuroscience and physics consensus in 2026, facing three stacked hurdles: Max Tegmark's thermal decoherence bounds (femtosecond-to-picosecond collapse in warm wet brains vs. millisecond neural timescales), underground Gran Sasso experiments (Donadi et al., Nature Physics 2021) ruling out the simplest parameter-free Diósi–Penrose gravitational collapse model via absent spontaneous X-ray emission, and lack of any demonstration linking microtubule quantum coherence to behavioral consciousness. Intrigued interest persists on a strictly narrowed biophysical frontier—2024 experiments reported ultraviolet superradiance in tryptophan networks within microtubules (Babcock et al.) and anesthetic binding shifts in tubulin—which proponents cite as revisions, though demonstrating room-temperature optical excitons falls far short of macroscopic neural quantum computing or gravitational consciousness.

episodes.label: Tripartite Synapse & Astrocyte Gliotransmission Debate — Perisynaptic astrocyte processes act not merely as passive structural, potassium-buffering, and neurotransmitter-clearing support cells, but as active third partners of the 'tripartite synapse' that sense synaptic activity via Ca2+ elevations and release vesicular gliotransmitters (glutamate, D-serine, ATP) to bidirectionally compute and modulate synaptic plasticity.
episodes.notes: While the anatomical and metabolic importance of perisynaptic astrocytes (potassium siphoning, glutamate uptake via EAAT2, metabolic lactate support, and slow neuromodulatory gating of sleep/arousal states) is universally established, rapid vesicular 'gliotransmission' remains one of cellular neuroscience's fiercest active debates in 2026. Critics (Fiacco & McCarthy 2018) showed that IP3R2 knockouts eliminating somatic astrocytic Ca2+ waves often leave baseline synaptic transmission and LTP intact and questioned whether astrocytes express canonical SNARE vesicular-glutamate machinery; conversely, recent single-cell RNA-seq and optogenetic/two-photon studies (de Ceglia & Volterra, Nature 2023) identified a specialized subpopulation of glutamatergic VGLUT1-expressing astrocytes mediating rapid synaptic facilitation in specific hippocampal circuits—suggesting heterogeneity rather than universal gliotransmission.

episodes.label: Mirror Neuron Action-Understanding & Empathy Hypothesis — Premotor and parietal 'mirror neurons'—which fire both when executing a goal-directed action and when observing another individual perform the same action—provide an innate, automatic motor-simulation mechanism underlying action understanding, mind-reading, empathy, language evolution, and (when dysfunctional) autism spectrum disorder.

episodes.label: Phrenology & Lashley's Strict Cortical Equipotentiality — Two diametrically opposed historical extremes of brain organization: Franz Joseph Gall's phrenology asserted that discrete mental faculties sit in isolated cortical organs readable from skull bumps, whereas Karl Lashley's Mass Action and Equipotentiality laws asserted that higher memory and cognition are distributed uniformly across cortex so lesion volume—not anatomical location—determines behavioral deficit.
episodes.notes: Both extremes have been definitively superseded by distributed functional-network neuroscience: specialized cortical areas and cell-type microcircuits (V1, Broca/Wernicke perisylvian hubs, FFA, hippocampal place/grid cells) genuinely exist—refuting Lashley's strict equipotentiality—while higher cognition emerges from dynamic, overlapping large-scale networks rather than isolated skull-molded faculty bumps—refuting phrenology. Both survive in the Atlas as indispensable cautionary anchors because modern neuroimaging regularly lapses into 'neo-phrenology' (assigning complex social traits to single fMRI blobs) while uncritical deep-learning/connectome holism risks reviving Lashleyan equipotentiality.

episodes.label: Biased Bugs or Bounded Optimality? — Kahneman & Tversky's Prospect Theory, Evans–Stanovich Dual-Process Architecture & the 19-Country Replication vs. Gigerenzer's Ecological Rationality, Lieder–Griffiths Resource Rationality, De Neys's Logical Intuitions & Gal–Rucker's Loss-Aversion Audit
episodes.notes: Why does the same person buy fire insurance on Monday and a lottery ticket on Friday—and why do we turn fiercely risk-averse for gains yet suddenly gamble to escape a sure loss? This five-act adversarial deep dive examines behavioral science's most influential paradigm: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky's reference-dependent Prospect Theory (Econometrica 1979; Nobel lecture AER 2003), Jonathan Evans and Keith Stanovich's autonomous Type 1 vs. working-memory Type 2 Dual-Process refinement (2013), and Kai Ruggeri et al.'s landmark 19-country, 4,098-participant multinational replication (Nature Human Behaviour 2020) confirming 12 of 13 classic effects. Then four rival insurgencies take the stand: Gerd Gigerenzer and Wolfgang Gaissmaier's Ecological Rationality (Annual Review of Psychology 2010), proving fast-and-frugal heuristics beat complex multiple regression out-of-sample through the bias-variance trade-off; Falk Lieder and Thomas Griffiths's Resource-Rational Analysis (BBS 2020), deriving anchoring and rare-event overweighting as mathematically optimal algorithms under finite neural budgets; Wim De Neys (BBS 2022), dismantling strict fast-and-slow exclusivity by revealing rapid logical intuitions inside speeded dual-task trials; and David Gal and Derek Rucker (2018), exposing how status-quo inertia masquerades as universal 2:1 loss aversion. Pause twice for step-by-step math—first computing Prospect Theory's exact certainty, reflection, 14.5-fold rare-event, and USD 274 mixed-gamble flips, and second deriving the exact N* = 42 bias-variance crossover where equal-weight Tallying beats OLS regression plus a 162-subject pre-registered two-response trial power floor—closing with a disciplined 2026 synthesis and a stealth-jargon field guide for working behavioral researchers.

theory.canonical_title: Dual-Process & Prospect Theory vs. Ecological & Resource Rationality
theory.core_claim: Kahneman and Tversky's Heuristics-and-Biases / Prospect Theory and Evans–Stanovich Dual-Process Theory model human choice as an interplay between fast, autonomous heuristic intuition (Type 1) and effortful, working-memory-limited deliberation (Type 2), governed by reference-dependent value functions and nonlinear probability weighting; Ecological Rationality (Gigerenzer) and Resource Rationality (Griffiths, Lieder) counter that these same heuristics are adaptive, variance-reducing, or computationally optimal under real-world time, memory, and uncertainty constraints.
theory.verdict_2026: Prospect Theory's descriptive patterns remain remarkably robust in 2026—verified across 19 countries and 4,098 participants by Ruggeri et al. (Nature Human Behaviour 2020, replicating 12 of 13 classic effects)—making behavioral economics a dominant scientific paradigm, yet its classical cognitive interpretation is undergoing deep revision. Large meta-analyses (Gal & Rucker 2018; Yechiam 2019) challenged universal 2:1 loss aversion for small/moderate stakes, Wim De Neys (BBS 2023) dismantled the strict 'Type 1 = biased, Type 2 = logical' exclusivity dogma by demonstrating rapid 'logical intuitions,' and Resource-Rational analysis increasingly unifies both camps by deriving Prospect Theory's S-curve and fast-and-frugal heuristics from bounded Bayesian optimization.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Applied behavioral-science papers routinely treat System 1 and System 2 as two anatomically distinct brain modules (or reified homunculi) rather than functional modes, and assume every deviation from Expected Utility Theory proves human irrationality without checking whether the behavior maximizes accuracy under bounded cognitive cost or non-stationary natural statistics. Writers also still cite the 2:1 loss-aversion constant as a biological universal despite strong context, stake-size, and status-quo moderation.

historical_evolution.milestone: Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman map availability, representativeness, and anchoring heuristics and publish Prospect Theory (Econometrica 1979), overturning Expected Utility Theory.

Gerd Gigerenzer launches Ecological Rationality showing fast-and-frugal heuristics beat complex regressions out-of-sample ('less-is-more'); Kahneman publishes 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' (2011), popularizing System 1/System 2.

Evans and Stanovich tighten Dual-Process Theory into autonomous Type 1 vs. working-memory Type 2; Ruggeri et al. (2020) confirm cross-cultural Prospect Theory robustness while Lieder and Griffiths formalize Resource-Rational cognition (BBS 2020).

De Neys (BBS 2023) advances Dual-Process 2.0 centered on parallel competing intuitions and conflict monitoring; 'choice-architecture nudges' face sobering meta-analytic publication-bias corrections (Maier et al. 2022).

theory.falsification_criteria: Strict classical Dual-Process exclusivity is falsified whenever cognitive load or extreme time pressure leaves normative logical/probabilistic conflict detection intact; strict Ecological Rationality fails where simple heuristics systematically underperform learnable Bayesian cues in real-world stationary environments.
theory.stealth_support: Your study shows asymmetric valuation of losses vs. gains around a shifting reference point, probability overweighting of rare events, or systematic shift from heuristic error to normative accuracy when working-memory load is removed.
theory.stealth_refute: Your study finds fast-and-frugal heuristics outperform full weighting out-of-sample (Ecological Rationality), logical conflict detection fires automatically under extreme time pressure (dissolving strict Type 1 vs Type 2), or loss aversion disappears when status-quo inertia is controlled.

head_to_head.theory_a_prediction: Intuitive Type 1 errors (base-rate neglect, framing, 2:1 loss aversion) stem from architectural cognitive biases that diminish under deliberation; normative integration beats simple heuristics.
head_to_head.rival_b_prediction: Apparent biases track environmental uncertainty and computational-time budgets optimally: fast-and-frugal heuristics beat full-information models out-of-sample under high cue redundancy, and conflict-detection signals occur rapidly inside intuitive processing.

episodes.label: Attachment Theory (Bowlby & Ainsworth) — Human infants possess an evolved attachment behavioral system that maintains proximity to responsive caregivers as a 'secure base' and 'safe haven,' crystallizing internal working models of self and others (categorized as secure, anxious/ambivalent, avoidant, or disorganized) that shape emotion regulation and relational expectations across development.
episodes.notes: Attachment Theory remains the dominant developmental paradigm for caregiver–infant socioemotional bonding in 2026, powerfully backed by cross-cultural Strange Situation studies, foster-care institutional deprivation trials (Bucharest Early Intervention Project), and adult dimensional attachment research (anxiety vs. avoidance axes). Significant refinements have pruned earlier deterministic overclaims: behavioral genetics and longitudinal cohorts (NICHD SECCYD, Fraley & Roisman) show that infant attachment is only moderately stable into adulthood (r roughly 0.15–0.25), is shaped bidirectionally by infant temperament and broad socio-ecological stress rather than maternal sensitivity alone, and functions better as continuous dimensional spectra than rigid lifelong personality boxes.

Cross-cultural developmental anthropology (Heidi Keller), twin studies, and long-term NICHD/Minnesota cohorts refine attachment into a dynamic, multi-caregiver, gene-by-environment relational model.

episodes.label: Multicomponent Working Memory & Cognitive Load Theory (Baddeley / Sweller) — Baddeley and Hitch propose that active online cognition operates via a capacity-limited multicomponent architecture—an attentional Central Executive coordinating domain-specific Phonological Loop, Visuospatial Sketchpad, and Episodic Buffer stores—while Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory deduces that instructional design must minimize extraneous load so finite working memory can build long-term schemas.
episodes.notes: Limited-capacity active maintenance and its direct link to complex learning (Cognitive Load Theory's worked-example, split-attention, and expertise-reversal effects) form a dominant, well-replicated pillar of cognitive and educational psychology. Mechanistically, however, Baddeley's discrete 'buffer boxes' face major competition from Nelson Cowan's Embedded-Processes model (working memory as the currently activated subset of long-term memory inside a ~4-chunk focus of attention) and Bays/Ma continuous-resource models (flexible precision allocation rather than fixed slots), while commercial 'working-memory brain training' transfers (e.g., dual n-back boosting fluid IQ) have overwhelmingly failed rigorous active-control meta-analyses (Melby-Lervåg & Hulme).

theory.canonical_title: Multicomponent Working Memory & Cognitive Load Theory (Baddeley / Sweller)
theory.core_claim: Baddeley and Hitch propose that active online cognition operates via a capacity-limited multicomponent architecture—an attentional Central Executive coordinating domain-specific Phonological Loop, Visuospatial Sketchpad, and Episodic Buffer stores—while Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory deduces that instructional design must minimize extraneous load so finite working memory can build long-term schemas.
theory.verdict_2026: Limited-capacity active maintenance and its direct link to complex learning (Cognitive Load Theory's worked-example, split-attention, and expertise-reversal effects) form a dominant, well-replicated pillar of cognitive and educational psychology. Mechanistically, however, Baddeley's discrete 'buffer boxes' face major competition from Nelson Cowan's Embedded-Processes model (working memory as the currently activated subset of long-term memory inside a ~4-chunk focus of attention) and Bays/Ma continuous-resource models (flexible precision allocation rather than fixed slots), while commercial 'working-memory brain training' transfers (e.g., dual n-back boosting fluid IQ) have overwhelmingly failed rigorous active-control meta-analyses (Melby-Lervåg & Hulme).
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Educational papers frequently treat George Miller's classic '7 plus or minus 2' span as raw working-memory capacity (ignoring chunking and Cowan's true unchunked limit of ~3–4 items) and circularly infer 'high cognitive load' from poor test scores without independently measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane load. Cognitive-training papers also routinely conflate near-transfer practice gains on trained span tasks with broad far-transfer gains in general intelligence.

episodes.label: Embodied & Grounded Cognition vs. Amodal Symbolic Representation — Embodied and Grounded Cognition (Barsalou, Varela, Lakoff) holds that human concepts, language, and reasoning are constitutively grounded in sensorimotor simulations and bodily states rather than manipulated as abstract, amodal symbols in a disembodied language of thought (Fodor, Pylyshyn).
episodes.notes: By 2026, the sharpest empirical cleavage runs between weak/moderate grounded cognition—now well-supported via hub-and-spoke semantic architectures (Patterson & Lambon Ralph) linking amodal anterior-temporal convergence hubs with modality-specific sensory-motor spokes—and radical/social-metaphor embodiment, which suffered catastrophic replication failures (e.g., Strack's pen-in-mouth facial feedback failing Wagenmakers' 17-lab Many Labs test, warm-cup social warmth failing Lynott et al., and power-posing hormones failing Ranehill/Garrison). Meanwhile, the stunning semantic competence of disembodied text-only Large Language Models (LLMs) has dramatically reinvigorated distributional/amodal symbolic accounts of abstract meaning (Mahon & Hickok), keeping the boundary between sensorimotor grounding and statistical-symbolic structure fiercely contested.

episodes.label: Theory of Constructed Emotion (Barrett) vs. Basic Emotion Theory (Ekman) — Basic Emotion Theory (Ekman, Izard, Panksepp, Keltner) posits a small set of evolutionarily conserved, pan-cultural affect programs (e.g., anger, fear, joy, disgust, sadness, surprise) with dedicated neural circuits and universal facial/autonomic fingerprints; Lisa Feldman Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion counters that emotions have no biological fingerprints and are instead ad-hoc conceptual categorizations constructed predictively from domain-general interoceptive 'core affect' (valence and arousal), context, and learned cultural emotion concepts.
episodes.notes: Affective science remains locked in a vibrant, unresolved paradigm contest in 2026, with neither extreme securing total victory. Barrett's side scored major empirical blows via meta-analyses showing high physiological variability within single emotion labels (Siegel et al. 2018), poor one-to-one mapping between posed facial muscle movements and real-world inner feelings (Barrett et al., Psychological Science in the Public Interest 2019), and indigenous cross-cultural studies (Himba, Trobriand) showing forced-choice universality collapses under free labeling. Basic/functional emotion theorists (Cowen & Keltner, Adolphs, Mobbs, LeDoux's survival-circuit revision) hit back with large-scale natural-video machine-learning studies revealing ~20+ cross-culturally recognizable vocal/facial expression blends and conserved subcortical defensive/appetitive circuits in animals—pointing toward a middle-ground 'functional emotion state' view separating conserved subcortical survival circuits from culturally constructed conscious feeling labels.

episodes.label: Massive Modularity Hypothesis (Santa Barbara Evolutionary Psychology) — The human mind is not a domain-general blank-slate processor, but a 'Swiss Army knife' comprising hundreds or thousands of genetically specified, informationally specialized cognitive modules (such as cheater detection, kin estimation, and mate-value calculators) sculpted by natural selection in the Pleistocene Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness (EEA).
episodes.notes: While evolutionary psychology's foundational rejection of pure cultural blank-slatism and recognition of evolved perceptual, social, and motivational predispositions are widely accepted, the strict 'Massive Modularity' architecture of Tooby, Cosmides, and Pinker is heavily challenged and under broad revision in 2026. Neuroanatomy and developmental biology (Karmiloff-Smith, Buller, Anderson's 'neural reuse,' Barrett's 'evolutionary developmental psychology') contradict hardwired Pleistocene cortical organs: human neocortex exhibits extreme developmental plasticity, massive gene-for-structure conservation, and continuous neural recycling of domain-general circuits, while cultural evolution (Henrich, Heyes's 'cognitive gadgets') proves that flagship supposedly innate modules—reading, theory of mind, causal reasoning, imitation—are largely culturally assembled atop modest domain-general cognitive starter kits.

episodes.label: Ego Depletion & Limited Willpower Resource Model — Roy Baumeister's Strength Model of Self-Control proposes that acts of volition, impulse inhibition, and difficult choice draw upon a single, domain-general, finite metabolic resource (later hypothesized to be blood glucose) that becomes temporarily depleted ('ego depletion'), impairing subsequent unrelated self-control.
episodes.notes: Ego depletion became one of the centerpiece casualties of psychology's Replication Crisis and remains heavily challenged and theoretically replaced in 2026. Carter and McCullough (2014) exposed severe small-study publication bias in the original 2010 meta-analysis; the 23-lab Registered Replication Report (Hagger et al. 2016, N = 2,141) found an effect statistically indistinguishable from zero (d = 0.04); the massive 36-lab multi-site test led by Baumeister's own collaborator Kathleen Vohs (Psychological Science 2021, N = 3,531) found at best a tiny, fragile effect (d = 0.06–0.08) failing preregistered significance; and the blood-glucose refueling mechanism was conclusively refuted (Kurzban 2010; Vadillo et al. 2016). Modern self-control science (Inzlicht, Shenhav, Kurzban) replaces the 'fuel tank' metaphor with opportunity-cost, motivational-shift, and Expected Value of Control (EVC) models of mental fatigue.

theory.core_claim: Roy Baumeister's Strength Model of Self-Control proposes that acts of volition, impulse inhibition, and difficult choice draw upon a single, domain-general, finite metabolic resource (later hypothesized to be blood glucose) that becomes temporarily depleted ('ego depletion'), impairing subsequent unrelated self-control.
theory.verdict_2026: Ego depletion became one of the centerpiece casualties of psychology's Replication Crisis and remains heavily challenged and theoretically replaced in 2026. Carter and McCullough (2014) exposed severe small-study publication bias in the original 2010 meta-analysis; the 23-lab Registered Replication Report (Hagger et al. 2016, N = 2,141) found an effect statistically indistinguishable from zero (d = 0.04); the massive 36-lab multi-site test led by Baumeister's own collaborator Kathleen Vohs (Psychological Science 2021, N = 3,531) found at best a tiny, fragile effect (d = 0.06–0.08) failing preregistered significance; and the blood-glucose refueling mechanism was conclusively refuted (Kurzban 2010; Vadillo et al. 2016). Modern self-control science (Inzlicht, Shenhav, Kurzban) replaces the 'fuel tank' metaphor with opportunity-cost, motivational-shift, and Expected Value of Control (EVC) models of mental fatigue.
theory.common_paper_blindspot: Management, behavioral-economics, and health-psychology papers still routinely cite Baumeister's 1998 chocolate-radish study or the discredited 'hungry judge' parole study (which was heavily confounded by case scheduling order) as proof of a literal willpower battery, ignoring the Hagger 2016 and Vohs 2021 multi-lab null/near-null replications and the collapse of the glucose hypothesis.

historical_evolution.milestone: Roy Baumeister, Ellen Bratslavsky, Mark Muraven, and Dianne Tice launch Ego Depletion with the famous radish-vs-cookie persistence experiment; Gailliot et al. (2007) claim blood glucose is the physical willpower fuel.

Robert Kurzban dismantles the glucose-depletion physiology on brain-energetics grounds; Evan Carter and Michael McCullough re-analyze Hagger's 2010 meta-analysis and reveal severe publication bias driving apparent d ~ 0.62 down near zero.

Hagger et al. (2016; 23 labs) finds d = 0.04; Kathleen Vohs et al. (2021; 36 labs, 3,531 participants) runs a gold-standard multi-lab sequential-task test finding d = 0.06 (non-significant under preregistered criteria), confirming the classic lab effect is negligible or absent.

Cognitive-fatigue research shifts to Michael Inzlicht's Process Model (motivation/attention shift from 'have-to' to 'want-to'), Amitai Shenhav's Expected Value of Control (dACC), and genuine prolonged-work neurochemical fatigue (e.g., prefrontal glutamate buildup over 6+ hours, Wiehler et al. 2022).
